findings.title: Runtime-drawn-model limitation not specified in any task's `model_dimension_note`
findings.description:
The slice design's success criterion states: "the **runtime-drawn-model limitation is stated where the recommendation is produced** (asserted: the note is present in output, including `--json`)", and the design's per-recommendation note section requires that "Where a step draws its model at runtime (a 180 pool), the note states that the threshold **cannot** track the drawn model — the recommendation does not apply to that step."

T9's `model_dimension_note` bullet (line 147) only requires the config-time model+threshold pairing half of the criterion; the drawn-model/180-pool sentence is absent from T9, from T10's content assertions (which only assert the note is non-empty), and from T16's CLI assertions. A junior implementer building exactly to this breakdown will ship a note that satisfies every task checklist but silently omits half of an explicitly asserted success criterion. Add the drawn-model sentence to T9's note spec and a content assertion to T10 (and ideally T16's `--json` check).

findings.title: Malformed `judge:` block failure-mode row is claimed covered but exists in no task
findings.description:
The design's Failure Modes table has a row: malformed `judge:` block → "fall back to `resolve_thresholds`' documented merge; **flag the target**; WARNING naming the template; test: malformed judge block → flagged, not silently defaulted."

The Coverage Check (line 287) asserts this row is "inherited from `resolve_thresholds`, exercised in T8". Reading T8 (lines 129–141), its five bullets cover direction bands, floor gating, unversioned refusal, and registered/unregistered template reads — there is no malformed-block test. T7's `read_current_thresholds` spec likewise only handles the unregistered → `None` + WARNING case; it never specifies the flag-the-target/WARNING behavior for a malformed block. Either add a malformed-fixture test to T8 (plus the flag/WARNING step to T7) or correct the coverage claim — as written, the breakdown overstates coverage of a design-required failure row.

findings.title: T7's numbered precedence list is self-contradictory as literally ordered
findings.description:
T7 specifies `classify_direction` "in this precedence order" with step 1 = `n < floor → INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` and step 4 = `match_rate <= tighten_rate → TIGHTEN` that is "reachable even if `n < floor`". Taken as a literal ordered cascade — which is how the list is presented — step 1 always fires first for below-floor cells, making step 4 unreachable for `n < floor` and directly violating the task's own success criterion ("a below-floor cell with low match rate returns `TIGHTEN`, not `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`") and the design's "tightening is not floor-gated" rule.

The prose after the list tries to reconcile this ("checked first only for the loosening path"), but a junior AI implementing the numbered order mechanically will get it wrong, and the resolution is buried in parentheticals. Rewrite the precedence so the ordering itself is correct — e.g. (1) unversioned → `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`; (2) `match_rate <= tighten_rate` → `TIGHTEN` (floor-ungated); (3) `n < floor` → `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`; (4) `match_rate >= graduate_rate` → `GRADUATE`; (5) else `HOLD` — and drop the contradictory annotations. (Note: the design's own Direction Bands table has the same row-order tension, so the task is faithfully reproducing a design flaw — but a task's job is to be unambiguous at implementation time.)

findings.title: Context Summary's "Suggested order" misnumbers the task ranges
findings.description: The Context Summary says "graduation + offers (T9-T12), then CLI shells + config keys (T13-T16)". Actual task numbering: T9/T10 are `recommend_thresholds` (the recommendation report), T11/T12 are the graduation registry, T13/T14 are residual offers, T15/T16 are CLI, and config keys are T5/T6 (deliberately sequenced early). The body of the task file follows the design's order correctly; only this summary sentence is stale and could mislead a reader about where config keys belong.

findings.title: A `**Commit**:` marker after all 17 tasks
findings.description: Every task ends with a `**Commit**:` line. The markers are plain lines (correct format) and each sits after a tested unit thanks to the test-with pairing, so none is premature — but placement is mechanical rather than at genuinely working points. This is acceptable as-is; consolidation (e.g., only after each implement+test pair, which is in fact what happens) is already effectively satisfied, so no action is required.
